transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Thank you for seeing me, doctor. Ever since that car drove into the crowd, even little sounds make me feel like I’m back there and I jump out of my chair or drop things. I just can't seem to shake this feeling.
Since the accident, have you been having nightmares, flashbacks, or avoiding places or reminders of it, and has this been going on for more than a month?

Yes, during the day it’s like a film on repeat in my mind, and at night I wake up in a panic with those same terrible images in my head. I've also been avoiding downtown, the senior center, and Mass because being near streets or crowds just terrifies me. But it hasn't been a month—the accident happened last week, so I've been living like this for about seven days now.
Have your symptoms been getting better, staying the same, or getting worse since the accident?

They haven't gotten any better at all, and the feelings have stayed constantly intense and overwhelming since it happened. If anything, it feels like it's getting harder to cope day by day because I'm so exhausted and isolated in my apartment. It just feels like it's wearing me down.
Have you had any dissociative symptoms since the accident, such as feeling numb, detached, or like things around you are unreal or happening in slow motion?
No, I haven't really felt numb or detached, and things don't seem like they are in slow motion. In fact, everything feels far too real and overwhelming for me right now.
Have you been able to sleep at all since the accident, or are you having trouble falling asleep or staying asleep because of the fear and replaying images?

I'm having terrible trouble sleeping, doctor. I lie awake staring at the ceiling for hours, and when I finally nod off, I jerk awake with my heart racing and those awful images of the street fair in my head. I just never feel like I’ve really slept.
Did these symptoms start within minutes to hours after the accident, or did they begin later that day or the next day?
They didn't start immediately in the minutes right after it happened. They really began developing in the days right after the accident, and it has been going on like this for about a week now.
Have these symptoms been present for less than one month, or have they continued for longer than a month?
Yes, it has been much less than a month. The accident only happened last week, so I've been dealing with all of this for just about seven days now.
Have you had any period of feeling completely unable to remember what happened during the accident, or do you remember it clearly?

Yes, I actually have some big blank spots in my memory from that day. I can remember setting up the booth, and then suddenly I was holding someone’s hand on the ground, but I can't piece together what happened in between. No matter how hard I try, I just can't remember how I got from one moment to the next.
Have these symptoms lasted less than one month since the event, or have they continued for more than a month?
It has definitely been less than a month. The accident happened just recently, and these feelings and reactions started right after and have only been going on for about a week now.
Have your symptoms been improving at all, or have they stayed severe for more than a month since the accident?

No, they haven't improved at all, but it hasn't been a month yet since the accident only happened last week. For this past week, these feelings have stayed completely intense and constant without any real relief.
Have these symptoms been getting better over the past few days, or are they still very intense and not improving at all?

They are not getting any better at all and remain extremely intense. It's been about a week since the accident, and I am still constantly on edge, jumping at every little noise and feeling unable to leave my apartment.
Did these symptoms begin within minutes to hours after the accident, or did they start later and have they continued for more than a month?

They started in the days right after the car crash, rather than within minutes or hours. They definitely haven't been going on for more than a month, since the accident only happened about a week ago.
Did your symptoms begin right away within minutes to hours after the accident, or did they start later and keep going for more than a month?

They didn't start right away in those first few hours, but rather in the days immediately following the crash. It has only been about a week since it happened, so it definitely hasn't been a month yet.
Did your symptoms start within minutes to hours after the accident, or did they begin later in the days afterward?
They didn't start right away in the minutes or hours after the crash. They began building up in the days right after the accident, and it has been going on like this for about a week now.
Did your symptoms start within the first 3 days after the accident, or did they begin later than that?
Yes, they started within those first couple of days right after the accident happened. It's been about a week now that I've been feeling this way.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed an acute trauma-related syndrome within days of a qualifying traumatic event (car driven into a crowd), with intrusive re-experiencing, nightmares, marked avoidance, hyperarousal/startle, severe sleep disturbance, and partial amnesia. Symptoms began within the first few days and have persisted for about one week, which is most consistent with acute stress reaction (F43.0) rather than a longer-duration post-traumatic stress disorder.
